EICMA 2026 • MTPeak Stole Some of the Spotlight at EICMA 2026 With Insane Power and Retro Looks on Three Wheels
This Mobile Home Is the First-Ever to Feature a Quad Loft, and It's a Winner
19 photos
Photo: The RV Hunter
No one ever invented an industry first just for bragging rights, though they too must come in handy every once in a while. Kropf Park RVs, an industry leading manufacturer of park tiny houses and prefabs, has just unveiled the industry's first-ever quad-loft mobile house.
Called the Island 6478QP, it's part of the Island series of park tinies, which Kropf describes as "customized comfort." They're the most budget-friendly floorplans Kropf offers in basic spec, but each can be customized to an insane degree, until it becomes as fancy – and as expensive – as the premium options in the catalog.
For 2027, Kropf is unveiling an Island that boasts an industry-first quad-loft, allowing it to offer maximum sleeping capacity of ten people – eight of whom will be crashing upstairs, in a giant loft that nonetheless offers some privacy as well. Far from feeling like a can of sardines on a quad-axle and home-like design, this park tiny is actually good-looking and surprisingly spacious.
Built on a heavy-duty custom trailer with four axles, this Island home comes in at 43 feet (13.1 meters) of total length and 12 feet (3.6 meters) of width. It's a park tiny certified as a Park RV, which means it's designed to stay put on location and only travel by special towing rig and with special towing permits.
Photo: The RV Hunter It's a mobile house in the strictest sense, but mobility is limited because of its widebody design. In return, it offers more space inside, truly residential features and appliances, and thanks to that quad-loft, a very high sleeping capacity.
The quad-loft is the cherry on this park house-shaped cake: the first loft in the industry to run the entire length of the home, from tip to front end. Hunter from The RV Hunter says in the video tour below that Kropf is looking to patent the construction method of that loft, which would make sense.
The best part about this extended loft is that it does more than just offer space for four full mattresses, and actually creates a sense of privacy, to the point where you can talk about four bedroom spaces upstairs. It does that by inserting a larger piece of furniture between each pair of mattresses, thus offering sleeping and storage for all the people using these spaces, and one window in each space.
Photo: The RV Hunter The first space is also the larger one and could be equipped with a kiddie playroom space, in case of families looking to turn the entire upstairs into the children's space.
Meanwhile, the grown-ups will be downstairs, and Kropf doesn't disappoint here. Entrance is done directly into the living room space, equipped with a pull-out sleeper sofa and couch and an entertainment wall with a large-screen TV.
The open-plan kitchen takes up the front of the trailer, with a large U-shaped cooking block that integrates a peninsula that doubles as a four-person dining area, a separate walk-in pantry with a coffee hutch, and a massive double-door fridge and freezer tucked under the loft, next to the sofa. If you're counting novelties with this floorplan, the walk-in pantry is also a first for an Island model, and an excellent addition for a floorplan that caters to such a large party.
Photo: The RV Hunter Finishes include dovetail joinery on the full-extension drawers, thermafoil counters (upgradable to solid surface), soft-close hinges, adjustable shelves on all the upper cabinets, real tile backsplashes, and only residential appliances. Even in a floorplan that prioritizes sleeping space, Kropf delivers the best, so you get a four-burner cooktop with a large griddle section, a large oven, and a full-size microwave.
The main bedroom is at the opposite end of the trailer, offered standard with a king bed with overhead cabinets and smaller overhead cubbies. At the foot of the bed is a full wardrobe with a chest of drawers, prep for a second TV, and lots of natural light coming in through the window you won't block if you choose not to have that TV.
The bedroom gets light through windows on three sides, but you also have the option to have the entire rear wall of glass, by adding sliding doors and maybe an optional porch.
Photo: The RV Hunter The only bathroom available is located across from the solid staircase to the loft. It's more on the compact side, but it still offers a plumbed toilet, a nice fiberglass shower with gliding glass doors, and a porcelain sink on a vanity with integrated storage. Knowing it would have to service up to 10 people, Kropf does its best to add extra storage, including a linen closet and a smaller medicine cabinet over the toilet.
The unit shown below is more or less standard, so while it's nice to look at, it's not the nicest looking you can get from Kropf.
Photo: The RV Hunter That's the biggest selling point of an Island park home, according to the manufacturer : "an impressive list of standard features with endless upgrade possibilities to make sure your park model has all the comforts you desire without paying for any you don't."
This will come at a price, obviously. There's no MSRP or sale price mentioned for the display unit below, but I came across a slightly different 6478QP with a sale price of $136,845.
Via // The RV Hunter
